The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. Weighing attacking F3 directly versus just building my own wall, I decide the shoulder-hit style separation, like G4, could isolate F3 from G6, but F3 should still live easily near the bottom right corner. Given the complexity, I'll settle on playing E3 as my move.

Tracing through the atari exchanges, I see black's chain getting split awkwardly while my groups end up separated too — not ideal either way. D3 seems to preserve shape better and keeps E5 connected through D4/D5, so I'm leaning toward just playing E3 directly despite the uncertainty.
